description: Ex-IAF Shahak sold to Argentina in 1982 as C-713 and repatriated to the museum; presented in the markings of Shahak 159 with 13 kill symbols and carries both Israeli and Argentine roundels. Construction number CJ42 per spottingmode. True identity is the Argentine serial; the painted 159 is a marking not a proven identity.

Ex-Chilean Air Force J-747 construction number S4/U/3276 quoted as ex-RAF XF445. Displayed in Royal Jordanian Air Force markings and carries no serial on the airframe; Israel never operated the Hunter.
Construction number 13983. Displayed wearing the false serial 272; the true airframe is 270.
Construction number 13826. Ex-US Navy A-4F transferred to Israel.
Construction number 13349. Ex-US Navy A-4E transferred to Israel after 1967.
Construction number 20710. Early IAF Cobra.

Rebuild of a crashed Auster presented in the Mandate-era civil registration VQ-PAH; no Israeli military serial and no construction number recorded by spottingmode. ABPic records the airframe as Auster J/1 Autocrat VQ-PAH construction number 627. True identity unestablished so tail_number left blank.
Construction number 8538.
Construction number 32227. IAF twin-engined Huey.

Construction number 17667. Served as the airborne command post for Operation Thunderbolt at Entebbe in July 1976 and later housed the museum heritage film theatre. Condemned in the February 2022 disposal; the forward fuselage was sawn off and retained behind the display fence for a future Entebbe exhibit while the rest of the airframe was scrapped. Recorded as retained nose section only.
Construction number LD-489.
Construction number 285.

Construction number 16767; also carried the civil marks 4X-FPN. Named Masada. Repainted overall white during the 2021-22 refurbishment in a scheme it never wore in service and its doors were locked to visitors.
Construction number U206-01536.
Construction number 278. Displayed wearing the false serial 212. Locked to visitors after the 2022 refurbishment.
Construction number 30. IAI rebuild of the Fouga Magister.
Construction number 74. Displayed wearing the false serial 216.
Construction number 77.
Construction number 33307; also carried the civil marks 4X-FNZ.
Composite airframe presented in the Mandate-era civil registration VQ-PAU. No single true identity can be established so tail_number is left blank.
Construction number 2016.
Construction number 3113.

Construction number 6952; presented in the Mandate-era registration VQ-PAR. Grounded around 1990 because of damage to its wooden wings and named in the 2022 Ynet report among the airframes considered for disposal.
Construction number A044. IAF airborne early warning aircraft. A second Hatzerim E-2C serial 942 construction number A042 is recorded by spottingmode as removed and is not included.
Construction number 3920.
Construction number 4822. Flight test airframe of the IAF flight test centre Manat.
Construction number 3461. Cutaway display airframe with transparent panels showing the interior.
Construction number 2594. The Super Phantom re-engine demonstrator; displayed wearing the false serial 229. True identity 334.
Reconnaissance Phantom. No construction number recorded by spottingmode.
Construction number 4023. One of the three F-4E(S) long-range oblique photography Phantoms built for Israel.
Construction number 4020. Upgraded Kurnass 2000 standard.

Construction number 6V-4. Block 10 airframe and the first F-16 to land in Israel on 2 July 1980 at Ramat David. Flew Operation Opera against the Osirak reactor on 7 June 1981 piloted by Amos Yadlin and later accumulated 6.5 aerial victories over Lebanon in 1982 - a world record for the type. Retired 2015 and displayed with its kill markings.
Construction number 4020.
Construction number 55.992. Early IAF helicopter.
Construction number 58.1595. Displayed as 07; spottingmode records the true IAF serial as either 25 or 26 and it cannot be resolved so tail_number is left blank.
Construction number 65.084.
Construction number 89-0550D.
Construction number 110-0598D.
Construction number B01. Displayed wearing the false serial 301. A second Hatzerim Kfir TC2 serial 310 construction number B10 was recorded by spottingmode as removed to Colombia and is not included.
Construction number 47; also quoted as 451/01. Reconnaissance Kfir known as Prism.
Construction number 178. Long displayed as a gate guard at the museum entrance.
Construction number B01 as recorded by spottingmode; ABPic quotes construction number 01.
Construction number 74.
Two-seat Kfir converted from a Mirage IIIB airframe. No construction number recorded.

Ex-United States Marine Corps F-21A adversary aircraft leased from Israel in the 1980s and returned. Recorded by spottingmode as 999764/03 construction number 29. No IAF serial applies so tail_number is left blank.
Second Lavi technology demonstrator prototype. The programme was cancelled in August 1987. Its unpainted composite surfaces were noticeably weathered at the 2022 reopening.
Construction number 332. First jet fighter type in IAF service.
Construction number quoted as 234 by spottingmode; a contributor comment on the same page argues for 218 instead. Neither reading is confirmed.
No construction number recorded by spottingmode.
Construction number 214. Displayed wearing the false serial 11.
Construction number 173.
Displayed as 40; some sources identify the airframe as ex-RAF WA905 but the IAF identity is not established so tail_number is left blank. Long used as the museum gate guard.
ABPic records construction number 2173.
No construction number recorded.
No construction number recorded.
Recorded by spottingmode as a T.7 and a half - the Israeli hybrid with a T.7 forward fuselage and F.8 tail.
Night fighter. No construction number recorded.
Construction number 5582.

Presented as the Iraqi MiG-21 flown to Israel by Munir Redfa on 16 August 1966 in Operation Diamond and operated by the IAF as 007. The museum airframe was sent to the United States for evaluation and it is not established that the same airframe returned; a contributor note records it as ex-Iraqi 534 while the museum comment thread states the real origin is unknown. Retained as 007 pending better evidence.

Construction number 0390324522. Syrian Air Force aircraft flown to Israel by a defecting pilot on 11 October 1989 and given an IAF number. A March 2019 visitor inventory reads the number as 2781; spottingmode gives 2786 and is preferred because it carries the construction number.
Construction number CJ-06. Displayed wearing the false serial 158; the true airframe is 111.
Construction number D151; also carried the civil marks 4X-FAE. The February 2022 disposal list named a Nord among the aircraft condemned so this airframe needs re-verification.
Construction number S-01. Israeli-built Mirage 5 derivative.
Construction number 769. Airframe only - fuselage frame without covering.
No construction number recorded.
Construction number 111-36126. Photo-reconnaissance version of the P-51K.
Displayed wearing the false serial 41; the true airframe is 53.
Construction number 18-5252.
Construction number 18-7760.
Construction number 646; also carried the civil marks 4X-SVY. Displayed wearing the false serial 02.

Construction number 75-5096; recorded by spottingmode as 2752/52. The museum silver Stearman burned out on the ground in February 2015 through poor maintenance and was rebuilt from parts of two airframes. Since 2022 the museum airworthy aircraft are parked inside the operational area of Hatzerim and are brought to the display only for special events. Tail_number left blank because the rebuilt identity is a composite.

Czechoslovak-built Bf 109 derivative and the first IAF fighter type. The serial is painted in Hebrew as 120 with the letter dalet. Reported by Ynet in May 2022 as standing behind the display fence in an area closed to the public awaiting repainting and refurbishment.
Construction number 6256. Displayed wearing the false serial 05.
Construction number 125.
Construction number 138.

Construction number 1788. Syrian Army aircraft captured in Lebanon in 1982 and evaluated by Israel as 907. Also wears Syrian markings and the serial 1333; the genuine Syrian serial of this airframe is 1335.
Construction number 6499. Israeli naval helicopter.
Construction number 1969. Displayed wearing the false serial 03.
Displayed wearing the false serial 05 in a black colour scheme. No construction number recorded.
Construction number 30. Named Hamashhit - the Defiler.
Construction number 95. Named Big Brother.
Construction number 4. Two-seat night fighter named Phantomas.
Ex-RAF SL653 per the Wikipedia exhibit list. IAF serial written 20-28. Displayed wearing the false serial 26.

Construction number CBAF/171351; ex-RAF TE554. The Black Spitfire flown by Ezer Weizman; IAF serial written 20-57 and the aircraft is displayed as 57. Maintained in airworthy condition and since 2022 parked inside the operational area of Hatzerim rather than on the museum display line.
Construction number 6S/223490; ex-RAF EN145 per the Wikipedia exhibit list. IAF serial written 20-78 and displayed as 78.
Construction number 006.
Construction number 84-7666. Displayed wearing the false serial 14.
Construction number 88-17025. Displayed wearing the false serial 25.
Construction number 1694. Note that the IAF serial 334 duplicates the serial of the museum Super Phantom F-4E; the two are unrelated airframes in different IAF number series.
Construction number 71. Israeli-operated testbed; the type became the IAI Westwind after IAI bought the design.
Construction number 516999339. Ex-Madagascar Air Force airframe acquired from IAI via Romania in 2011.
Construction number 3507. Ex-Polish Air Force airframe displayed in Egyptian Air Force markings; Israel never operated the type.

Construction number V0699; ex-South African Air Force 255. Displayed in Lebanese Air Force markings as L158; also reported as ex-Swiss J-1139 which is inconsistent with the SAAF identity. The painted L158 is a marking and not this airframe.
Construction number 726; ex-Swiss Air Force J-1516. Displayed in Iraqi Air Force markings as 353; the painted serial is a marking not an identity.
Syrian Air Force airframe 1033 displayed in Egyptian Air Force markings. No construction number recorded.
Construction number 1956; British civil registration G-AHAY. Displayed in IAF markings as A-13.

Construction number 182-720; British civil registration G-BDZZ. The yellow Harvard displayed as IAF 001 and kept airworthy; since 2022 parked inside the operational area of Hatzerim and brought to the museum only for special events.
Construction number 20555; US Army serial 68-15021. Displayed in IAF markings as 444.

Construction number 0040; USAF serial 73-0098. Delivered to Israel and allocated the IAF serial 398 but never taken up in service; the museum displays it in the markings of Baz 695 with kill symbols. Neither 398 nor 695 is this airframe operational identity.

Construction number 2087; US civil registration N285RA. Donated to the museum by Boeing in 2008 at the initiative of 69 Squadron veterans and displayed in IAF markings as 3401. Reported by Ynet in May 2022 as standing behind the display fence in an area closed to the public awaiting repainting.
Construction number 834; US civil registration N6564K. Displayed in IAF markings as B-61.
Construction number 2094; US civil registration N7850C. Displayed in US Navy markings as V34. Wikipedia gives the Bureau Number as 69355.
Construction number 15809; ex-Venezuelan Air Force 0053. Displayed in Egyptian Air Force markings.

Ex-Czech Air Force Mi-24D reported as serial 4010 construction number M344010 and acquired by Israel for evaluation; sources disagree on whether it arrived in 2004 or 2011. A March 2020 visitor report found it stripped and awaiting rebuild rather than on the display line. Not listed at all by spottingmode. Tail_number left blank because the identity chain is unverified.
